To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a single blood marker (FibroTest) is as accurate as the combination of two blood markers and liver stiffness measurement (FibroScan) to diagnose liver fibrosis and non-invasive tests are more accurate than the clinical scoring systems in patients with chronic liver disease.

1. The diagnostic value of the FibroTest is not significantly different from that of the FibroScan in the main causes and stages of chronic liver diseases (CLDs), including viral hepatitis, alcoholic liver disease, and non-alcoholic fatty-liver disease.

(i) the combination of blood markers and liver stiffness measurement (LSM) by transient elastography (FibroScan) is more accurate than the best blood markers and LSM by FibroScan alone, and (ii) the combination of FibroTest, Forns’ score, LSM and AST/platelet ratio index is more accurate than FibroTest, FibroMeter, Forns’ index and LSM.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an innovative diagnostic method for liver fibrosis in chronic liver disease.
the development of a novel approach for the diagnosis of cirrhosis.
the development of new and improved methods of detecting liver disease and the use of these methods to improve the management of patients with liver disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in the presence of cirrhosis, the risk of developing HCC is high enough to justify the use of surveillance, but in the case of non-cirrhosis the risk is low enough that the benefit from surveillance is unlikely to outweigh its cost and inconvenience.
the FibroTest is the best blood fibrosis test in NAFLD.

, in the context of NAFLD, the use of blood fibrosis biomarkers is not recommended for the diagnosis of fibrosis and the exclusion of cirrhosis, but it is recommended for the prediction of advanced liver fibrosis in patients with biopsy- proven NASH.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a single test combining Fibrotest with Fibroscan (Fibrotest + Fibroscan) is more accurate than Fibrotest, Fibroscan, or other fibrosis tests, for diagnosing fibrosis in the main causes
of chronic liver diseases, and is a reliable and accurate tool for diagnosing cirrhosis.

we have demonstrated that the combination of blood markers and transient elastography (TE) provides a very accurate diagnosis of liver fibrosis in patients with the main causes of cirrhosis (HCV, HBV, alcohol, NASH) and is more accurate than any other single test.

we have shown that a single test combining blood fibrosis markers with transient elastography is more reliable than other fibrosis scores for diagnosing fibrosis in the most frequent causes of chronic liver disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the combination of blood fibrosis markers with liver stiffness measurements is more accurate than either of the two tests used alone, and that this combination can be used to determine the need for liver biopsy in patients with non-alcoholic fatty disease.
liver biopsy remains a gold standard for the diagnosis of liver disease, and that the non-invasive methods are not yet ready to replace liver biopsy for this purpose.

a single test combining blood fibrosis markers (Forns score) and liver stiffness measurement (LSM) by Fibroscan (LSM+Forns score) is more accurate than the other fibrosis tests, including Fibrotest, ActiTest, and APRI, for the main causes of CLD.
